title: XXI: The New England Holiday

teacherSummary.text: Election Day brings a festive crowd: Native people, sailors and townsfolk. Hester's face is calm, as if this were the last day of her ordeal. The ship's captain tells her that Chillingworth has booked passage on the same ship. Chillingworth smiles at her across the square.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Hester was clad in a garment of coarse gray cloth” slowly and put it in my own words: On the public holiday, Hester wears the same coarse gray garment she has worn for seven years. Next, craft. I notice the contrast between a festive day and her unchanging dull dress. The strongest word is “coarse”: it shows the rough, humble clothing she has accepted as part of her penance. Then, effect. Why does the narrator stress Hester's plain gray clothes at the holiday? My answer: The narrator stresses Hester's plain gray clothes at the holiday because they make her almost invisible while the letter still stands out; secretly she is planning to escape, so her calm look hides a great change.
